text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--The East Asiatic Company (EAC) is to meet major institutional investors on Thursday to discuss its controversial Asian production of Paraquat herbicide -- banned in Denmark -- and its sales to military-ruled Burma.
--A survey shows consumer confidence on the rise again after a fall in May.
--Den Danske Bank says that the government's economic policy is too expansionist.
--The main opposition Liberals will seek to win 13 municipalities and four county councils in the November local authority elections, seen as a dress rehearsal for next year's general election.

--EAC is one of about 11 European companies targeted for a consumer boycott by an international committee critical of the Burmese military government's human rights record. Among the others are Sweden's Ericsson, French oil company Total, Premier Petroleum, ING Bank and ABN Amro.
